question.text: A particle travels along a straight path such that its speed v decreases as a linear function of position s, starting at 20 m/s when s = 0 and reaching zero at s = 30 m. Find the acceleration of the body at the position s = 15 m.
conditions: velocity varies linearly with displacement s

solution.approach: Write velocity as a linear function of displacement, then use a = v(dv/ds) at s = 15 m.

steps.text: Velocity falls linearly from 20 m/s at s = 0 to 0 at s = 30 m; write v as a function of s.
Differentiate v with respect to s; the slope is constant.
Use a = v(dv/ds) with v = 10 m/s and dv/ds = −2/3 to find the acceleration.

common_mistakes.text: Using the starting velocity 20 m/s instead of the velocity at s = 15 m, giving a = 20 × (−2/3) = −13.3 m/s².
Dropping the negative sign on the slope and writing a = 10 × (2/3) = 6.67 m/s².
